title: Frankl's union-closed sets conjecture
formal: For every finite set \(U\) and every family \(\mathcal F\subseteq 2^U\) containing a nonempty member and closed under union, is there an element \(u\in U\) belonging to at least \(|\mathcal F|/2\) members of \(\mathcal F\)?
definitions: The power set \(2^U\) consists of all subsets of U. A family is a set of distinct subsets, with no multiplicities. Closure under union means that A and B in the family imply that their union is also in it. The frequency of u is the integer \(|\{A\in\mathcal F:u\in A\}|\). Empty members are permitted, but the family consisting only of the empty set is excluded.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated proposition, with all its quantifiers and hypotheses. Verification of finitely many parameter values does not establish the universal assertion.
why: A basic closure principle for set systems, connected to information inequalities through entropy methods.

context_blocks.text: Gilmer obtained a positive universal frequency bound by comparing the information in random members with the information in their union.
Costa and Sadhu report a bound above 0.38288 in 2026. Their target and result still distinguish this progress from the conjectured one-half threshold.
